title: Solubility of Krypton and Oxygen in Water and Aqueous Uranyl Sulfate Solutions at Elevated Temperatures
authors: C. J. Anderson, R. A. Keeler, S. J. Klach
experimental_method: Stainless-steel 550 ml vessel with 275 ml solvent, Kr-85-tagged krypton at tracer level plus oxygen overpressure, heated to 100-300 C; simultaneous vapor and liquid samples withdrawn, Kr determined by radioactivity, dissolved gas by gas law and sample volume.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature of the liquid measured to +-0.1 C (Chromel-Alumel with potentiometer); pressure gage 0-2000 p.s.i.; no uncertainty on solubility values in Table II (text gives a regression for K(T) with standard deviation 0.218e5 for water).
quality_remarks: Scan exponents partly blurred: K exponent glyphs of 5.93 (Kr-14 s2), 2.03 (Kr-15 s3), 1.75 (Kr-17 s4 oxygen) look like 6 and 8.74 (Kr-17 s2 oxygen) like 9 in the image; all entered as 10^5, consistent with neighbouring rows and the text layer is also unreliable here. Run '13' printed without 'Kr-'. Kr-8, Kr-9, Kr-12 have no oxygen solubility measurement. Mole fraction of Kr in liquid is not tabulated, only K. Uranyl sulfate solutions are out of the six-ion set; Table I composition used for them.
not_extracted_tables: Table I (experimental conditions summary: composition, ranges; not data rows; composition values used in mapping)
